utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ryneveld.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Before I continue with the examination-in-chief of the present witness, Halil Morina, I thought I ought to inform the Court and my friends that, with the Court's permission, we propose to change the order of the next two witnesses, to reverse them. Mr. Agron Berisha, who is a specialist, a medical doctor, who has been here since the beginning of this trial, is concerned to get back to his patients, and so we've let the amici know of our proposed change in order, so that he will follow the cross-examination of this witness. So that just number 7 and 8 are being reversed. That is, with the Court's permission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Is it necessary to remind this witness that he's still under oath? Have we done that or ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Perhaps you would like to remind him.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Examined by Mr. Ryneveld: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Morina, just before we start, I want to remind you, sir, that you have taken a solemn declaration to tell the truth in these proceedings. Do you understand that, sir?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Could you say that again, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, last Thursday you had told us some things leading up to the fact where you and your family decided to hide by a stream near your house. Do you recall telling us that?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I believe you also told us that the stream was located fairly close to your home, and from there, you could see what was going on; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, could you tell us what was happening to the inhabitants of your village, of Landovica?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 26th, there was murder and the houses were burnt down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the other villagers of your community -- you and your family hid. What did the rest of the people who were not killed, what did they do, if anything?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They left the village. Some of them remained, but part of them left towards Srbica and Povjanik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you explain to the Court, if you would, please, could you describe the method by which they left? Was it an organised, slow arrangement or did they leave in haste, or what? How did they go?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the firing started, there was alarm in the population.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what effect did that have, if any, on their departure?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no particular -- there was nothing particular. They just left. They just went away. There was nothing particular.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they have luggage with them or were they --

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, only the clothes they had on their bodies. They couldn't take anything else with them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How much time elapsed between the beginning of the shelling and the departure of the villagers?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The bomb -- the shelling was from 11.00 until 3.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when did the people start to leave?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: From 9.00 until 10.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, while you were in your hiding place, can you describe to us, after the shelling stopped, what happened next?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The -- the jeep, a military vehicle, came a few minutes after the shelling, and I was with my brother and my -- and his wife. He came with me. And there was shelling going on and firing into the air.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've told us on Thursday afternoon that a number of infantry troops and police arrived; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone appear to be in charge of these police and soldiers?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't tell who was their chief. I saw them coming to the village and setting fire to it from the Gypsy neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You speak Albanian. Do you understand any Serbian?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever, from your vantage point, hear any Serbian being spoken by anyone?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I heard, when they came to set fire to my own house and to the neighbouring house, speaking Serbian.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall hearing anyone giving orders of any kind?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: When they first came to shell the village, I heard them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to give us any particulars of what you heard?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I heard them coming.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On Thursday, I believe you told us, and I believe you repeated it again this morning, that they were killing people. Do you remember a particular incident whereby people in your village were killed?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I saw them while they were burning the village. They killed a Gypsy. And when they came down, they killed Avdi Gashi, an Albanian. And a paralysed woman, they set fire to her in her own home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When those killings occurred, could you overhear anything at all?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard fire shots. I could hear the automatic shots.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did the troops stay in your village?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until 7.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you and your wife and brother remained in your hiding spot until that time?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We stayed about three hours, two or three hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what time did you leave your hiding spot, if at all, and where did you go and why?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We left the hiding spot about 4.00. I can't be more precise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We went to a nearby brook where the house of a neighbour was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. What then?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then we went to see what was happening, what had happened in the neighbouring houses. Then I went -- we went to our home. We saw that it was burnt.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your own home had been burned?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Two homes were burnt. Two Drama, two cars.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "Two Dramas," he says, "two cars."

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only the livestock remained. Everything had been razed to the ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this is about your own personal property you're speaking about?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say it was razed to the ground, were you able to occupy your home any more at that point?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was nothing left to use in my own home. In my brother's home, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So where did you go?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We went to my brother's home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That late afternoon, early evening, did you notice the condition of the mosque?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was on the next day that I noticed it. On the 27th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I assume that you and your wife and brother stayed at your brother's house that night. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Early the next morning then, sir, did you go looking around the village?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. First I went to the neighbouring house and I saw there 13 dead bodies lying on the floor. Then we went to search in other houses of the village to see if there was anyone left. We didn't find anyone. And then we returned back home. No: First we went to bury -- we went to search for our family. Thirty-nine members they were. We didn't find them. Until 11.00, we looked round in the fields, in the brook, everywhere. We didn't find them. They had left for Prizren.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you say you found 13 bodies. Did you notice any other bodies as you went around the town?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know any of the bodies when they were alive?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us who, if anyone, you can recall having been killed?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The day that they were killed, Ismet Gashi was the first, then his mother. You have written the names in my statement: Suzana, Fatime, Nikmini, one and a half years old.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, Witness. Just because you have given a statement listing those names, until you tell this Court about them, the Court isn't going to know, so I have to ask you the names. I can't assist you with that. So please tell us. Just because it's in your statement doesn't mean that we know about it until you tell us today, okay?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now I don't remember the names. Three years have passed. Ismet Gashi, Fatime, I remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, sir. I'm not asking you to remember all of the names, but you knew the people who were killed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only two I didn't know. They were guests from Kukes. I didn't know them by name or otherwise. The 11 others, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, sir, as you went around the village, you earlier told us that there was about 120 houses in your village before the attack; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to give an estimate to this Court as to how many of those houses were destroyed as a result of this attack?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Seventy-five per cent were burned and destroyed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I asked you earlier about the mosque. You told us you saw it the next day, the 27th. We're on the 27th. Was it at this time you saw the mosque or was it later?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw it on the 27th, at 11.00. We came from the field and went back home. Then a group of soldiers came and examined the corpses, and three of them went to the mosque. They entered the mosque. They had white ribbons on their arms and they started to fire at the mosque, to shell it. In ten minutes, I heard the explosive, a blast, and the minaret fell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, perhaps you could explain exactly what you saw. You said they started to shell it. Can you explain to us what you saw before the explosion? Describe to us what occurred.

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They went there by car. They got down out of the car, they entered the mosque, they placed the mine, and I heard the explosion, and then I saw it toppling down. Nothing else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So when you say "shelled," you don't mean with a tank; you meant that they carried something inside? I think you said it was a mine or something?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mines. They had something -- they were carrying something in their hand. No, they didn't use tanks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. All right. You had used the word "shelling," so I thought I'd ask you to explain what they meant by that. They carried something into the mosque; is that correct? Did the soldiers leave then?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how long after they left the mosque did you hear the explosion?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as a result of that explosion, you then saw the minaret fall onto the roof of the mosque; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you say "soldiers," again, sir, just for sake of clarification, how did these soldiers arrive? What kind of vehicles and what were they wearing from which you could deduct that they in fact were soldiers?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They came by Pinzgauer cars, and there was a Zastava car. Before they shelled the mine, they came and examined the corpses. Then they shelled the mine. They came back and borrowed a private Zastava, on which they loaded the bodies of the dead people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, I understand -- we'll get to that in just a moment, but the purpose of my earlier question, sir, was: You've described these people who arrived as soldiers. What were they wearing that made you to believe that they were soldiers? Could you describe their clothing for us?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The army uniforms, no other uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And these were regular army uniforms, were they, sir?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was my impression.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I tried this on Thursday. I don't believe I got an answer. Can you tell me today, do you remember what colour those uniforms are?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The usual Serb army uniform, that colour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. All right. Now, you told us -- now, these soldiers had arrived at about 11.00, I think you told us. Did they stay, or did they go away and come back?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They stayed awhile, examined the bodies that were up in the house on the hill, shelled the mosque, and left. Again they came at around 12.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And just so that we're clear, when you say "shelled the mosque," you're now giving that expression to what you've told us earlier about going into the mosque and setting off an explosion. There's no additional shelling going on.

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So at about 12.30 or so on the 27th of March, soldiers returned or more soldiers arrived; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Before you leave there --

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just a moment. It may be helpful, to see if we're more successful with this, to know what a Pinzgauer is.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Might I have Exhibit 17, please. Might the witness be shown Exhibit 17.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you'll recall on Thursday you were shown a series of photographs - I think it was four pages with numbers - of what appear to be vehicles, from 1 to 15. I would like you to look through those 15 photographs very carefully, and if you could, tell the Court what you mean when you say a Pinzgauer, if a Pinzgauer is shown in any of these 15 photographs comprising the four pages of Exhibit 17.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: So just -- perhaps, Mr. Usher, you could show the witness personally first before we put it on the ELMO. Just let him have a look at it up close. Show him all four pages so that he can make a selection.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the Pinzgauer.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: All right. The witness has selected one of the photographs. I'm waiting for --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you have instructed the usher to put a photograph which contains 5, 6, 7, and 8. Do you see what you mean as a Pinzgauer by number on this photograph? Could you tell us what number it is and point to it. Could you take the pointer, Witness - thank you - and if the Pinzgauer is on the set of four photographs from which you've selected --

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This here. This is what I meant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're pointing to what looks like number 7; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, he's pointed at 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: For the record, is that a troop carrier? Would you describe it as that?

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Yes. It's a large lorry or a truck. "Troop carrier," that's probably the best way to describe that. Does that assist the Court? May I move on?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you've told us that at about 12.30, soldiers returned; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what, if anything, did you see them do when they returned at 12.30 on the 27th of March?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't do any harm, only took away the corpses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And again, the people that came back at 12.30, were they again army?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were carrying light weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were they the same kind of uniforms that you told us about earlier, or different?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anybody appear to be in charge?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had a komandir. I didn't know who he was. A commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And could you hear the commander give any instructions to the soldiers?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They went to that house where the dead were, and I heard him telling them, "Come with me. Let's go to that house where the bodies are," and they went there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you see them do? Did you see them collect the bodies?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did they do it slowly or was there any particular method by which they collected these bodies?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very quickly. They quickly pulled out the bodies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, sir, that's the 27th. The bodies were collected. Did the soldiers return later that day or the next day or was that it?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't come back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you and your wife and brother stay in Landovica?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We stayed there until the 30th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 30th of March?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of March.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened after that?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then we didn't have anything to live on, and then we went to Srbica and then Skenderaj, and then we stayed there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us earlier that your -- that the villagers had fled, and you were looking for members of -- the 39 members of your family. Did they return at that point?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they did not. They went to Prizren.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said you had nothing to live on, is that correct, back in Landovica?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you went to Srbica?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before going to Srbica, we let the cattle go to the pastures to eat something because we didn't have anything to feed them, and then we went to Srbica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you find your family there?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, no, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you stay?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Srbica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you got to Srbica, were there any other refugees there?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We found there about 800 inhabitants of Pirana.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this Pirana, that's the village that you told us about on Thursday that was three kilometres away that had been attacked before your village; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So those villagers left Pirana and you found them in Srbica when you arrived on the 30th of March?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Srbica, yes, Srbica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, you stayed in Srbica, I take it, for some time, did you?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: For a while, yes. And in Srbica, there were Serbs and Albanians together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And I take it at some point you left Srbica. How did that come about?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Albanian -- the Serb neighbours told the Albanians to get rid of the HOS of the Albanians, because they might fare by being troubled, and they brought buses there. In an hour, we got on the buses and went to Albania. My brother went to his family in Prizren.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who arranged for the buses?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you want to leave?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: What could we do? There was no other way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what did you do?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We got on the buses. The police were accompanying the buses -- before the buses from Podrum of Landovica to granica was -- we travelled. There was a long convoy of people, with tractors, Dramas, and stuff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's stop there for a moment. There were a number of buses that were prepared -- they were brought by the Serbs, and who got on those buses?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We Albanians, the refugees from Pirana and Landovica. We were the ones.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you get to choose where the buses were going to take you?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were two or three buses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me restate my question. Did you have a choice as to where these buses were going to take you?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They wanted to take us to Albania, and then we could go wherever we wanted from there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you were told you were being taken to Albania; is that right, sir?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: En route you say you saw a convoy. Can you tell us how long that convoy was that you passed with your buses?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 25 kilometres long.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you tell the ethnicity of the people that were in that convoy? You've told us tractors and trailers. Were there people on foot as well?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were all Albanians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were some of them on foot?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, some of them were on foot. They had little wagons with them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your evidence, sir, you told us earlier that the police did something. I wasn't quite sure what you meant by that. What were the police doing?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they didn't do anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Ryneveld --

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Morina, before we move -- you said that the Serbs arranged for the buses. Who do you mean by "the Serbs"? Are they Serb neighbours or Serb armies or Serb policemen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They weren't -- it was not the neighbours. No. They were civilians.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Civilians. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: I'll clarify that issue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know why it was that the civilians arranged for the buses? How was it that that came about?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The army gave the orders for the refugees to leave, because of their neighbours. So that their neighbours wouldn't be damaged because of all the bombarding, they should leave. Serb neighbours that helped the Albanians because they had been living there together for so long. They didn't want the Albanians to get hurt. That's why they helped.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And you say it was the Serb army that gave the orders?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see them give the order, but villagers from my village told me that we have to leave because the Serbs had taken orders to get rid of the refugees. They came and let us know that we had to leave the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. You've told us that you saw police along the way. Where was it that you saw police?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the entrance to Prizren, they didn't do anything up to Zhur, to the buses. They just opened the way. When we arrived in Zhur, we got off the buses and then we had to walk.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how far was Zhur from the Albanian border?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't be very precise. Maybe three, four, maximum five kilometres. I can't be accurate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you want to go to Albania?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't want, but we had to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened at the border, if anything, sir?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They took away our IDs, our passports.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did that happen? Who took away your IDs and passports?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe to us -- so you get to the border, and can you describe what happened personally, what happened to you?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We arrived at the border. We lined up and then we handed over our IDs. I handed over mine and my wife's. And then that's it. Nothing happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you hand it over? Was it requested of you?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They asked us to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did they do with the ID, if anything?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They threw them in a pile on the ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they ever returned to you?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a couple more questions, sir, before I'm through. Backing up to the beginning, sir: At any time when you were in Landovica, are you aware whether there had been any NATO bombing of your village?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there wasn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you leave your village?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because the houses were burnt. Everything was burnt down. There was nothing to live on. If they find that we were out in the streets, they might kill us, and so we had to leave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you want to leave your village?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: How could I want to leave the house? We had no other choice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Morina.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: I believe I have no further questions at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Milosevic. Cross-examined by Mr. Milosevic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You said at the very outset that Landovica is a purely Albanian village, that there are no Serbs in it.

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Later on, at the insistence of the Prosecutor, you corrected yourself, and you said that there were a few Romany houses too.

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: According to the information I have, Landovica was a village that was half Albanian, half Romany. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That's not true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Percentage-wise, how many Romany were there?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were 20 houses in all who were Roma.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you live in Landovica nowadays?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where are those Roma now?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some of them are in the village, and some of them are not there any more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many of them are there in the village now?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Half of them are there, and half of them are gone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that on the 26th, you were watching from the hills and you saw Pirana, the village of Pirana, being burned.

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that Pirana is three kilometres away from your house or, rather, from that hill.

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that morning, when were you on the hill?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would ask the Judges to give me permission to talk. I -- I have someone from Pirana who has five children, and we went to get the children so they wouldn't be killed. And we went down the road to Srbica, and then we took the children with us, all of them, by car. And that's where we saw it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Answer the question, Mr. Morina. The question was: "On that morning, when were you on the hill?" Can you tell us approximately what time you were on the hill that morning?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] About 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Proceed, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you got off the hill, then you went down to collect these relatives from Pirana; right?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The children, yes, children.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How much time do you need to descend from the hill to your house?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Five or six minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you see from the hill that Pirana was burned?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that day, it was -- part of it had been burnt. Part of it, not all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But what did you see from the hill?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw smoke and flames.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you came to the conclusion on that basis that Pirana was on fire?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did somebody tell you that?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, no one did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that hill, when you were up there to watch, were there any military men there?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: With all the smoke and the flames, you couldn't see anyone at all, neither military people nor civilians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm talking about the hill that you were on.

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were alone there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But on the hill there was the army.

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, nowhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you collected these relatives from Srbica, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Back home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do with your relatives?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were not relatives. They were my children, my wife and my children. And there was an uncle there. At an uncle's -- an uncle's house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are talking about peasants from Srbica, from Pirana, that they were down there and that you went to collect them. That's what you said awhile ago.

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We went to Pirana to fetch the children, but they were not in Pirana. They had left Pirana and had gone to Srbica. That's why we went to Srbica. I took five of my nephews, along with my daughter-in-law.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you talking about the village of Gornja Srbica, or is it Donja Srbica?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is the distance between Landovica and Donja Srbica?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: About two, three kilometres. I can't be so precise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did I understand you correctly? From the hill, you descended to Donja Srbica, and you picked up your acquaintances and relatives; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the hill, I went home. I got my car to go to Pirana first. And they told me, "Don't go to Pirana. There is nobody there. Your children, your grandchildren are in Srbica." That's why we were there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how long did you spend in Srbica?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two, three minutes. Just picked up the children and left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you went back home?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were all these children with you at home?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were all at home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were not watching what was going on outside?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing. No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how much time did you spend in the house with the children before you heard the shooting?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Five minutes. Then I heard the shooting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, five minutes before that, when you walked into the house, you did not see anyone; right?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So at 9.00, you were on the hill, and from the hill you saw that Pirana was on fire. You are claiming that there were no military men on the hill. And then -- let me just see whether I have understood correctly what you have said. Then you went home, took the car, went to Donja Srbica, picked up your children. You say that Donja Srbica is three, four kilometres away. You picked up your children, you returned from Donja Srbica to your house, and then you did not see anything; and then, five minutes later, you heard shooting. And everything you described happened within one hour. Isn't that -- is that right?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please allow me to explain. Pirana was burnt on the 25th, one day before us, before our village. So everything happened on the 25th. On the 26th, then they started to burn our village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That, in fact, was his evidence when he was giving evidence on Thursday. THE ACCUSED [Interpretation] During the examination-in-chief, I heard that he came home from the hill, that he saw from the hill that Pirana was on fire, that he came home, and that at 10.00 he heard shooting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No. His evidence was that on the 25th, he saw the village on fire from the hill, and then on the 26th, the incident happened in Landovica itself when there was the shooting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when were you in Donja Srbica; on the 25th or the 26th?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 25th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A minute ago, you said that with your children, you came from Donja Srbica five minutes before the shooting started. You came to your house five minutes before the shooting started.

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's my mistake. Maybe I didn't give you the right date or the date for that. I should have given the date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. But I asked you how much time you spent in the house with your children, whom you brought from Donja Srbica, before the shooting started, and your answer was that the shooting started five minutes upon your entry into the house, when you came back from Donja Srbica with your children?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: He said that that was a mistake. Which day, Mr. Morina, so we have it right, which day was the shooting on in the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is the aim? On the 26th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: So on the 26th there was the shooting. Mr. Milosevic, I think we'll save time if we move on to the 26th, unless there's anything else you want to ask about the 25th.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do have something else to ask.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since it is clear that things do not seem to match here, the question is: When did you bring your children from Donja Srbica to your house? On the 25th or on the 26th?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 25th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How could the shooting start five minutes later, then?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No. He's answered that question. Let's move on from there.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He answered that he did not say the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You can comment on that in due course. Now, let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear that on the 25th - that is to say, the day when you say that part of Pirana was set on fire - did you hear that on the 25th, NATO had hit the gasoline station Fatani, in the village of Pirana?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know the gasoline station Fatani, in Pirana?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 25th, when NATO was bombing, they hit the gasoline station Fatani and this caused a fire. Nobody told you anything about that?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A few minutes ago, you said that all the time while you were in Landovica and in Srbica, you did not hear anything about NATO bombing; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't hear anything about it, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you did not see airplanes or bombings of any of the grounds near your village all the while while you were there?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see anything, no. I was at home and didn't see anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that from the 24th of March until the end of March, the time that you were there, NATO bombed the area in which your village is located, as well as Prizren and the environs, several times a day? Do you know about that or not?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: For Prizren, I know, but I didn't see it myself. I know about it. I hadn't -- I didn't see it directly myself, and I can't tell if I didn't see it myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you heard the bombing, I assume.

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I didn't hear it, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't hear the bombing either?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's go back to the 26th, then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, let me clarify something. I believe in answer to a question that you asked, he said that he didn't see it himself - that's the bombing - but he had heard of the bombing. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's exact. That's exact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: From whom did you hear? From whom did you hear about the bombing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I couldn't tell who was doing the bombing, whether it was from NATO or from the Yugoslav side. There was bombing, but I didn't really see it with my own eyes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Did somebody tell you about the bombing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Continue, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that in Landovica it was calm on that particular day when the four soldiers entered the village.

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then suddenly you heard shooting?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard shooting when we were in the house eating, having a meal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were those four soldiers when you heard the shooting?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were in the centre of the village; descended down the mountain, went to the centre of the village. I didn't see them either alive or dead with my own eyes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there a shop in the centre of the village?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a small shop.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the soldiers go to the shop?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't lie. I didn't see anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you thought about it, because you're talking about it now.

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand what you mean. Can you repeat the question, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you didn't see, but you're talking about an event which you didn't see, so I can only assume that you gave the matter some thought, as you're telling us about it now.

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see what happened. I'm telling you about what I saw, the damage inflicted on us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you about your opinion. What, in your opinion, was the reason -- what do you think the reason was that members of the KLA began shooting at those four soldiers? Why did they do that, do you think?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no KLA soldiers in our village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did the shooting? Who shot at the soldiers, then?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The person who got killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that a civilian was killed in the centre of the village on the occasion and that his name was Hajim Gashi.

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you now claim that that civilian shot at those four soldiers?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you: I didn't see them either alive or dead, but I heard that he killed them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they killed him?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you say that nobody else did the shooting, just the man who got killed himself?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you again: I didn't see it with my own eyes. I don't like to lie. That's not my habit. Since I didn't see or hear anything, I heard he was killed, and that's it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that three out of the four soldiers were killed; you heard that too, did you?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I heard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you heard the shooting?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't even hear the shooting?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't hear the shooting either, no. Because I told you: We were at home. All our family was eating then. We were at home. We didn't hear anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far is your house from the centre of the village?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: About one kilometre and a half. I can't be precise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And from one and a half kilometres away, you weren't able to hear the shooting?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. You can hear the shots, but the television was on, the children were there. We were a lot of people at home. There was a lot of noise. Even if there was a cannon, I wouldn't hear, not a rifle shot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Later on, did you learn, later on, from which houses they opened fire on the soldiers?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean those who got killed or the other soldiers?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At those who were killed.

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were killed there in the middle of the village. I told you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. But where -- did you happen to learn where the shooting came from? From which houses did the shooting come when they were killed?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The houses of Tahir Berisha. But I don't know how true that is that they fired from that house. I didn't see anything myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Apart from the shooting that was done from Berisha's house, did you happen to hear of any other house from where the shooting came?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: What can I tell you? I think I am telling you the truth. We were eating, having our lunch.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Morina, there's no need to repeat what you've said. If you didn't -- if you know of any other house from which there was shooting or you heard of any other house from which there was shooting, just say so. If you haven't heard of any other house, just say you haven't. Is that right? You haven't heard of any other house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't hear of any other house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the name of any -- of the other people who owned houses in the centre of the village?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are several houses in the centre of the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it was -- the shooting only came from Berisha's house; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That's what he said, as far as he knows or as far as he was told. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that there were no members of the KLA in the village.

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there weren't. Even if there were, they would have left. They would have told the people to leave. We didn't have any KLA soldiers in our village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That means that this KLA group came to Landovica from some other village. What village did that group come to Landovica from?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: He's said that they didn't have any KLA in the village. Now, that's his evidence. If you dispute it, Mr. Milosevic, you can call evidence of your own on the subject, but there's no point arguing it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm asking him whether he knows where they came to Landovica from, and that's quite a legitimate question, Mr. May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It's not when he has said that there weren't any. Now, if you want to make a point about the shooting, of course you can, but he says that there were no KLA in the village. Now, there's no point then asking him where they came from when he said there weren't any.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May, four soldiers coming to a village, to a shop to buy only juice are killed by shooting from the houses of that village, not by phantoms but by members of the KLA. Now, I am asking where these members from the KLA came from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, you can make the point as you have made it to us, and you can make it in due course and you can call evidence about it, but there's no point asking this witness where they came from when he says there were none. Now, unless you've got a different question about that, I suggest that we move on. You can ask him, if you wish, how it was -- yes. Go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear - because you say you saw nothing - did you hear that when they killed the three soldiers, they went up to another one that still showed signs of life and shot a round of gunfire? Did you hear about that?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I did not hear anything. And in the evening, my family left the house and took to the mountain. If I heard anything, I would have left also with the others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But did you hear that after they had killed those soldiers, they covered them with an Albanian flag? Did you hear about that event?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. To tell you the truth, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did the fighting go on between the soldiers and the KLA before the KLA entered the village?

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Your Honour, with respect --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It's the same point. He's denied that the KLA were there. You could put to him that he's wrong about that, but we can't really take it any further.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness said that there was no heavy shelling. That's one point he made.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the second point which you said was that it lasted from 11.00 until 1500 hours. So that means from 11.00 until 3.00 in the afternoon. Does that mean that the army targeted facilities from which they were being shot at or does it mean something else? It lasted a full four hours.

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the army targeted facilities from which they were being shot at; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not very clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, just a second, please. Mr. Morina, I just read your statement offered by the Prosecution. Did you once tell the Prosecution that the soldiers were killed by KLA and you changed your statements later? Is it true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I have never said that KLA was there. I can't tell you who killed them; I didn't see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Ryneveld, could you clarify on this?

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. As I indicated in that proofing, that in his original statement, there was reference to the soldiers having been killed by KLA. At the proofing session, this witness indicated that that was a mistake, that that was not what he said, and that's why I put in the proofing session that he amended his statement during the proofing session. I made it very clear so that that would not be hidden from the amici, the Court, or the accused that there was a previous statement wherein the witness did refer to KLA. But in that same statement, in fairness to the witness, he did indicate in that statement that there were no KLA in the village. So all I can conclude from that is that the witness told me that that was an error when the statement was taken, because consistently in that statement, later on in the same statement, he said there were no KLA. So for -- but in fairness to everyone, I thought I had to put in the proofing -- in the summary to the Court that that happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's quite clear. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can I just raise one matter, because it might assist Your Honour Judge Kwon on the matter? The statement said that it wasn't a haven for the KLA and never had been, which might be a different matter as to the origination of the KLA in relation to this incident. I just raise that out of completeness, the Prosecutor having raised the matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I think, Mr. Ryneveld, we accept the explanation that you have given and also what the amicus has said. You will have an opportunity to re-examine. The evidence must, of course, come from the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Absolutely. I might also indicate, this matter having been raised by the Court, would it be of assistance to the Court under these circumstances that you have the witness's entire witness statement?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: It's a matter of weight for the Court, and therefore, in fairness, the Court may be assisted by having a copy of that statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I think normally it would be made an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Thank you. Then I have copies of that statement here, and that's K0209157 is the ERN number, and I believe the amici and the accused have got copies of the statement, of course, that having been previously disclosed.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit P19.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Does that become an exhibit or not? I don't know. It does?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic. You were asking about the shelling on the 16th.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, and the witness has answered. He said that the army shot at the houses from which they were being shot at.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I have another question and it is this: Before, previously, did you ever go into the house? And let me tell you which one I mean. Across the stream, 200 metres away from the shop. That's the house I mean, in which the KLA had its headquarters. So across the brook or stream, 200 metres away from the shop, in the centre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Did you understand the question? What is being suggested is the KLA had headquarters in the village, 200 metres from the shop, and you were asked if -- well, first of all, if you agree there was a headquarters, and if so, did you go there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What headquarters? I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, I think we're going to get no further with this. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I asked whether he had ever gone into that house which was 200 metres from the shop, across the stream, in which the KLA had its headquarters. He did not give me an answer to that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: He didn't understand. He denies they had the headquarters. So let's move on to another question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear -- did you happen to hear, perhaps, if you didn't see, what the soldiers found in that house: maps, ammunition? What else? Did you hear about that?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't hear anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember - now, you must have heard this with your own ears - do you happen to remember that from the 25th until the end of March, NATO bombed the area your village is located in six times? Did you hear that bombing?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't have any NATO bombing in our village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you could neither see it from the village nor hear it from the village?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no NATO bombing in my village. We heard on television that the Landovica school was hit by NATO, but when we came to the village, the school was intact. It was misinformation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where, then, was the population from your village and the surrounding villages fleeing?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They went to various villages before going to Albania. Half the village went in the direction of Srbica, and then Petrova and Prizren. In Prizren, they stayed one month.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they fleeing across the Verbnice Pass?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I didn't see them, which way they took. I didn't escort them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you crossed the Verbnice Pass yourself. You mentioned that. You didn't mention the actual pass, but you said, "From Zhur, we went on to --" and most of the refugees exited through that crossing, through that pass; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, we're not talking about your village, but we're talking about the fleeing of the refugees from Verbnice Pass. Did you hear that some members of the KLA went that way too?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you, I don't know anything about the KLA. They were all civilians. They took to the mountains. They followed that road. I don't know. I didn't see them myself. I just heard that the people passed through those routes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. It's now 11.00. We'll adjourn for half an hour. Mr. Morina, remember, again, not to speak to anybody about your evidence, please, during this adjournment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In response to the Prosecutor's question what happened with the population, you answered, "Nothing in particular. They simply left." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's exact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Prosecutor insisted that you say how much time after the shelling started the villagers started to leave. You said that they left before the shelling. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We left before. It was five, five or six minutes before the shelling started that we got out, my family.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In response to the question when people started to leave and when did they leave, you answered, "Between 9.00 and 10.00," and you said that the shelling started at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How come 13 were then killed in the shelling if they left before 10.00 and the shelling started at 11.00?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were at home like I was, with my family, with Ismet Gashi, a lawyer, and we didn't see anything. They were -- people were all in their homes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You spend your entire life in Landovica; right?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stayed in Landovica from the 26th to the 30th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you lived in Landovica before that for many years; right?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. All my life I spent there, with the exceptional time I did my military service, which was two years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Precisely. That's just what I asked you. You spent your entire life in Landovica, and you said today here this morning that you do not remember a single name out of 11 of your fellow villagers for whom you claim were killed.

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some I remember. I said -- the adults, yes, I remember, but the young, the children, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you did not mention a single one except for Gashi.

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell you Ismet Gashi; his mother Fatime, the wife of my cousin, was killed. Zanja, the daughter of my cousin; and the child about one year and a half, two years old.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said, in addition to them, that one Roma were killed and one Albanian. So including that Roma and that Albanian, did you see who killed them?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The infantry troops killed them. When they burned the houses, they also burnt two bodies inside the houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see who killed them, though?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not, because we saw the dead bodies on the next day. Avdi Gashi, we saw him dead in his own house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what did you infer? What killed them?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think because of the killing of the four military soldiers, and the police and the army burned the village and killed them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You did not see that, how they got killed?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you left the village around 4.00.

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't -- I'm not clear. What do you mean by "4.00"?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Around 4.00. When you look at your watch and you see that it is 4.00 in the afternoon. It was my understanding that you said that you left the village then.

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We left on the 30th of March, around 4.00, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And immediately after that, you said that the army remained in the village until 7.00.

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How come you know that they stayed until 7.00 if you left at 4.00? Who told you that they stayed until 7.00?

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: With respect, Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: In fairness to the witness, I believe that the question, the previous question and this question are at cross-purposes. I believe that the witness has referred to the 30th of March, whereas the accused is now asking about the 26th of March. I just -- for clarification purposes, I didn't want this to go on. In fairness, the witness ought to be asked what date they're talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that in Landovica there were no members of the KLA, and now I'm asking you whether any of the citizens of Landovica was a member of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know of it. I don't know of any one of them being a KLA member. Maybe there were some. I don't know. But they didn't tell me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how do you explain, then, that after the war, in Landovica, the monument to Boro and Ramiz was destroyed? Wasn't it destroyed?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was put in place of this monument to Boro and Ramiz?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: With dead soldiers of KLA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From Landovica?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How could a monument be built to the dead soldiers of the KLA from Landovica if there weren't any in the first place?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The KLA -- I don't know. The KLA must have done that. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that the army, on the 27th, shelled the mosque.

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Afterwards you corrected yourself. You said that it had not shelled the mosque but that an explosive device had been planted there.

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The minaret fell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Only the minaret? If an explosive device had been placed underneath the mosque, how could the minaret only have fallen?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Can you answer that or not? If you can't, say so.

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. All of the minaret fell over the top and destroyed the top of the mosque too, the roof. It is a very thick layer. It's 40 centimetres thick.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. You said that the army, when it returned on the 27th to the village, did not cause any damage to anyone.

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I heard you. You said: When they returned, they did not harm anyone.

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Only on the 26th and the 27th. Nothing has happened during the other days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Then we've clarified these dates, that when the army returned, they did not cause any damage to anyone. You said that you found in Srbica 800 inhabitants from Pirana.

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many of you were there from Landovica?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Three: myself, my brother, and my wife.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Only the three of you from Landovica?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And 800 from Pirana?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then you said that all of you together went to Albania and that there were two or three buses there.

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were more than three. Five or six.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said two to three.

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Six, seven, I think. I can't be very precise. And my brother went to Prizren to take care of his family and I went to Albania.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Then two or three buses or six or seven buses. How did 800 of them, together with you, fit into even six or seven buses?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: But not everybody got on the buses. We were many.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that these buses were organised by civilians.

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but on the orders of the army, who had threatened them either to get rid of us or they would be held liable. Then they came to us and told us, "You have to leave Srbica, because we too will suffer."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that, after that, you saw a convoy 25 kilometres long.

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. From Podrum of Landovica to the granica - trucks, cars, trailers, a lot of people, Albanians - to the border.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that they were evacuated. I'm quoting your words: They evacuated them so that there would not be any damage due to the bombing, so that they would not be harmed by the bombing.

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what their purpose was, but I know that everybody left the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the explanation that you gave that they were evacuated so that there would not be any damage due to the bombing, that is your explanation. How is this explanation possible if there was no bombing at all?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, that's a comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In addition to the refugees that you were watching, were there any medical teams there as well who were helping people who were injured due to the bombing?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There -- there were some in Prizren. Some went to Albania.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see medical teams that were helping refugees? When these convoys were going, were they going by the convoys?

utterances.speaker: HALIL MORINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, before you go on, you put to the witness earlier that the explanation that he gave was that they were evacuated so that there wouldn't be any damage due to the bombing, presumably so that they would be safe from the bombing. When did the witness give that explanation? Was it in examination-in-chief?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, during the examination-in-chief, I should say, because that's the only thing we've heard here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. I just wanted to be clear.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I assume. Or he said it during the course of the morning here. But at any rate, you certainly have this on the tapes, that he gave this explanation.
